notes:
- Company: mid-market product analytics SaaS; heavy customer support volume (60k monthly conversations).
- Primary objective: reduce support response time & deflection via an LLM-powered assistant + searchable embeddings for KB.
- Started with Hosted API to validate quality and latency; now evaluating Redwood Dedicated for predictable unit costs.
- POC highlights: embeddings quality good on small KB; reranker latency sensitive during peak (they require p95 < 600ms).
- Cost workshop outcomes (2/15):
  * Batching: continuous batching expected to cut per-token GPU time ~25% on chat workload with 10-50 concurrent sessions.
  * Caching: prefix/KV caching for common prompts reduced repeated token generation by ~18% in sample traces.
  * Quantization: 8-bit PTQ for reranker candidate scoring reduced GPU memory footprint, allowing denser pods; slight quality delta (BLEU/ndcg drop within tolerance).
  * Unit economics: Redwood team provided a model comparing hosted usage vs dedicated reserved (with autoscale) across 3 volume curves; dedicated becomes ~40% cheaper at >= 40M tokens/month with 95% availability requirement.
- CTO quote: "If we can hit 40% cost savings and keep p95 under 600ms we can move to Dedicated."
- Risk: finance wants downside protections (min/commit tiers) and written runbook for fallback to hosted if Dedicated capacity issues occur.
- Security: SSO + KMS required; data residency for EU customers is a must (they are NA HQ but have EU customers).
- Action items captured in INF-1223 and SEC-451 (See drive docs).
use_case_summary: Support assistant + semantic search + reranking pipeline. Evaluate quality on historical transcripts; cost sensitivity high (mid-market margins). Need predictable monthly spend for budgeting.
poc_results_summary: Hosted POC: quality pass; observed cost variability on heavy days. After optimize workshop: estimated 20-45% cost reduction scenarios via batching + caching + 8-bit quant. Dedicated sizing suggests break-even at ~40M tokens/month. Latency targets: p50 <250ms, p95 <600ms (met in most tests).
